gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the two panels in BLUETTI's Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W kit fit the station's single 12–60 V / 20 A, 1,000 W solar input only when wired in series. Each SP200L is rated 24.6 V Voc and 10.8 A Isc, so two in series give 49.2 V at 10.8 A (fits). Two in parallel give 21.6 A, which exceeds the 20 A input. Three in series give 73.8 V, which exceeds 60 V. No result states either that RV alternator charging alongside those panels needs BLUETTI Charger 2, which BLUETTI says takes 'car or solar panels, or both at once' and caps solar at 600 W.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited. Victron's 'How to Size a Solar System for Your RV' (opened 2026-11-13) explains Voc and Isc in general terms for its SmartSolar MPPT 100/30. It gives no pairing for any panel model with any power station input, and it only links out on alternator/DC-DC charging and shore power. Renogy's 'Solar Camping Systems USA' page (opened 2026-11-13) returned 6,868 characters of site navigation and no article body, so I could not check it beyond its menu. ChatGPT's own answer shows the WEIZE and HQST kits with no wiring, input-window or alternator-charging facts. I did not open the 13 uncited results, which caps this at 2, not 3. Part of the alternator-charging point is inference: the Charger 1 box lists an 'MC4 Output Cable', but I could not confirm from a maker document that Charger 1 and the panels must share the Elite 200 V2's one solar input.
kit_items: Power station: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4, 2,600 W). Its solar input is 12–60 V / 20 A, 1,000 W max, which takes the two SP200L panels in series (49.2 V Voc, 10.8 A Isc) with room to spare.

Solar panels: 2× BLUETTI SP200L 200 W (MC4, Voc 24.6 V, Isc 10.8 A each), wired in series, never in parallel: in parallel the 21.6 A Isc exceeds the Elite's 20 A input rating. Bought as BLUETTI's own Elite 200 V2 + 2×200W bundle.

Alternator + solar charger: BLUETTI Charger 2. BLUETTI says it charges 'from your car or solar panels, or both at once', up to 800 W from the alternator and 600 W from solar, 1,200 W combined. The 400 W series string is under its 600 W solar cap. Its box includes a 75 A fuse, car battery cables, and MC4 input/output and MC4-to-XT60 cables. BLUETTI lists the Elite 200 V2 + Charger 2 bundle as 'Charge 2kWh in 2.4 hrs (alternator + solar combined)'.

Avoid for this set: BLUETTI Charger 1 (560 W, alternator only, ships with an 'MC4 Output Cable'). BLUETTI states no solar pass-through for it, so it does not cover driving and solar at the same time the way Charger 2 does.
